pages.text: "I will tidy up later!" Nils the little bear tossed the broom onto the shed floor after using it. The bucket rolled and the rope lay in a tangle. The floor was covered in things, but Nils was already outside.
Nils came into the shed with an armful of pinecones. "Ow!" He stepped on the loose bucket, slipped, and landed with a thump. Pinecones rolled everywhere.
Nils searched for his favorite pinecone, the biggest and plumpest one. He looked under the broom and lifted the tangled rope. "Where is my big pinecone?" Tears filled his eyes.
Grandpa Bruno stood in the doorway with firewood on his back. "Why is the shed so messy?" "...The things keep getting under my feet." Nils sniffled.
Grandpa put his broad palm against the shed wall. A row of pegs stuck out. "Count the pegs. One, two, three..." Nils looked between the wall and the floor. Six pegs, and six things on the floor.
"One peg, one thing!" Grandpa hung the broom on the first peg. Nils hung the bucket on the next one. A perfect fit! "Oh! There is more room on the floor!"
Excited, Nils hung things one by one. "One, look at what you are holding! Two, find its peg! Three, hang it up!" Up went the rope, up went the saw. The pegs filled one at a time.
Things hung side by side on the wall. Only one basket remained on the floor. The last peg was still empty too. "Grandpa, only this one is empty!" Nils looked up at it.
Grandpa lifted the basket, and something rolled out from underneath. The biggest, plumpest pinecone! "My pinecone!" Nils lifted both paws high above his head.
Nils hung the basket on the empty peg. Grandpa rubbed his back. Hang things in their places, and they will not get lost. "One peg, one thing!" Nils said, looking at the full wall.
